novel_features.name: Architecture-feature search
novel_features.description: Search HF for models by architecture feature (mtp, mla, moe, gqa, sliding-window, rope-yarn) — fields HF doesn't index, recovered from config.json + card text.
novel_features.rationale: Requires fetching and parsing config.json per candidate; no HF endpoint surfaces these features as filters.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs models with specific architectural capabilities (MoE, MTP-readiness, long-context attention) that HF's search UI cannot filter on.

novel_features.name: vs-current diff
novel_features.description: Diff a candidate model against the model the named agent currently runs, by reading data/openclaw.json directly.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local config knowledge no HF tool has — answers 'would this replace what I run today?' which is the whole product premise.
novel_features.why_it_matters: The single command that closes the loop between HF discovery and the operational decision to switch models.

novel_features.name: Backend-readiness oracle
novel_features.description: Verdict whether a model's architecture is supported by a target backend, citing PR numbers, commit SHAs, and wiki notes with source_checked dates.
novel_features.rationale: Bundled matrix with citations beats optimistic guesses; an honest 'no' beats discovering after a 30GB download.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before downloading any new model; catches incompatibility upfront.

novel_features.name: Bench-history join
novel_features.description: Join an HF model id with local model-eval-harness results to surface tasks run, scores, vs-baseline delta, and last-run date.
novel_features.rationale: Closes the discovery→eval loop by reading harness output the eval pipeline already produces; no other tool reaches into local eval state.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Stops the eval pipeline from re-running known losers on every refresh.

novel_features.name: Eval-candidate emitter
novel_features.description: Emit a list of HF candidates in the model-eval-harness input format directly.
novel_features.rationale: Wires HF discovery into the existing local eval pipeline as a one-liner.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when scouting a new base model — pipes directly into the harness without copy-paste.

novel_features.name: Watch + agent-notify
novel_features.description: State-file subscription with cron-callable poll; matches emit through the MC API alert pipeline as structured events.
novel_features.rationale: Passive intel, not just on-demand lookup; agents get notified about new uploads matching watched criteria without polling themselves.
novel_features.example: huggingface-pp-cli watch add unsloth --kind uploader --notify jarvis
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when monitoring a specific uploader, base model, or feature for new releases as part of intel automation.

novel_features.name: Quant-variant browser
novel_features.description: Surface GGUF quant variants of a base model with uploader rep, effective size, and quant-type classification — sorted by trusted-uploader allowlist + size filter.
novel_features.rationale: HF has no first-class quant index; requires base_model:quantized: tag filter + GGUF sibling parse + uploader allowlist heuristic.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when picking a quant for a target hardware budget; encodes a curated trusted-uploader heuristic (unsloth, bartowski, mradermacher).

novel_features.name: Multi-runtime probe
novel_features.description: Single-call structured runtime-shape covering TTY, JSON, state writability, live config presence, harness presence, backend-matrix age, rate-limit remaining, HF reachability, proxy presence.
novel_features.rationale: Agents call this once at session start and branch all subsequent calls on the result — replaces ~9 separate probes per session.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Required first call for any agent script; tells the agent what runtime constraints apply.

narrative.headline: A stack-aware model-intel CLI for local-inference rigs and autonomous agent fleets — not just an API mirror.
narrative.value_prop: Closes the loop between Hugging Face discovery and operational decisions: should this model replace what runs today, will it load on the chosen backend, has it already been benched. Every command is multi-runtime safe (TTY-agnostic, --json + stable schemas, exit-code semantics, flock-guarded state) so the same binary serves an interactive terminal and a containerized agent without per-environment forks.
narrative.auth_narrative: Anonymous read works for every public endpoint. Set HF_TOKEN (or use the cached token at ~/.cache/huggingface/token) for higher rate limits.

quickstart.comment: Probe the runtime first — agents branch all subsequent calls on this output.
Find quant variants matching your hardware budget.
Diff against the model the named agent runs today.
Verify backend support before a 30GB download.

troubleshoots.fix: Set HF_TOKEN to a Hugging Face read token from https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens. Anonymous limits are ~5K req/day; authed limits are much higher.
Pass --config-path / --harness or run from a directory containing data/openclaw.json or workspace/scripts/model-eval-harness. The CLI exits cleanly rather than crash when context is missing.
Bundled backend-support.json is stale. Override via --backend-support <path> or ~/.local/state/hf-cli/backend-support.override.json.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI whenever the answer to 'should I switch from what I run today?' would otherwise require a WebFetch dance through model cards, config.json files, GitHub PRs, and local config. The discovery half (find-feature, find-quants, model-card, backend-check, trending, derivatives, uploader-rep, compare-quants, doctor, schema, local) is universally useful with no setup. The stack-coupled half (vs-current, bench-history, eval-candidates, watch, watch-poll) lights up when the caller has a local agent config (data/openclaw.json shape) and a model-eval-harness layout — set HF_OPENCLAW_ROOT or pass --config-path / --harness to point at any compatible paths.

recipes.title: Should I switch?
recipes.explanation: Diffs candidate against the running primary model and surfaces only the delta fields.

recipes.title: Find an MoE with MTP that runs on llama.cpp
recipes.explanation: Architecture-feature search HF doesn't expose; returns only entries with backend-readiness verdict YES.

recipes.title: Pick a quant for 25GB hardware budget
recipes.command: huggingface-pp-cli find-quants Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --prefer iq4_nl,q4_k_m --max-size 25g --uploaders unsloth,bartowski,mradermacher --json --select id,quant,size_gb,uploader,uploader_rep
recipes.explanation: Sorted by uploader rep + size; --select trims output to the agent-relevant fields.

recipes.title: Has this been benched?
recipes.explanation: Joins HF id with local harness results — exits 6 cleanly if no harness data.
